size: Usually 3–4 m, rarely up to 5 m; very heavy
lives: Ground and water, rocky ridges, burrows
keys: By far the biggest and thickest snake here
Dark-edged olive-brown blotches on a paler background
Dark arrowhead on top of the head, edged with a pale line
Small smooth scales; heat-sensing pits along the lips

confuse.how: Much shorter (around 1 m) and fat for its length, with pale chevrons, not blotches; never more than a hand thick

behaviour: Ambushes at water and on game paths and kills by constriction: dassies, cane rats, guineafowl, small antelope. Spends cold months in an aardvark burrow or a rock crevice. The female coils round her eggs for two months and stays with the young for a while.
bite: Not venomous, but a big python has long curved teeth: deep cuts that bleed and can get infected. Clean the wounds and see a doctor.
memo: The arrowhead on the head: only the python has it.

size: Usually 70 cm–1 m, up to 1.2 m; very fat
active: Mostly at night, basks by day
keys: Thick body and broad flat head, short thin tail
Pale backward-pointing chevrons on yellow-brown to grey
Hisses loudly and long when disturbed (the 'puff')
Moves slowly in a straight line, like a caterpillar

confuse.how: Python grows far longer, has blotches and an arrowhead on the head, not chevrons
Egg-eater is slender with a small rounded head, and rasps its coils instead of hissing
Night adder stays under 45 cm, has an upturned snout and a dark V on the head

behaviour: Trusts its camouflage and does not move off: most bites in Africa come from people stepping on it, often on a path at night. Strikes fast, to the front or the side. Ambushes rodents, birds and toads.
bite: Severe pain and swelling within minutes, blistering, tissue damage; can kill if untreated. No pressure bandage (it makes the tissue damage worse): keep still, keep the limb at heart level, hospital fast. The polyvalent antivenom works.
memo: It won't get out of your way: torch on your feet at night.

keys: Small adder with an upturned, pointed snout
Dark V or arrow mark on the head
Dark rhombic blotches along a grey-brown back
Round pupil, unlike most adders

confuse.how: Bigger (to 60 cm) with a rounded, not upturned, snout
Egg-eater has a small rounded head and no V mark; it rasps its coils

behaviour: Eats almost only toads and frogs, so it is found where they are: around water, gardens and wet grass after rain. Puffs up, hisses and strikes when bothered.
bite: Pain and swelling, sometimes lymph nodes; no deaths known. The antivenom does not work on night adders and is not used: hospital for pain relief and watching.
memo: Upturned snout and a V on the head: the little toad-eating adder.

keys: Dark rhombic blotches, often pale-edged, on grey to olive
Dark V on the back of the head
Rounded snout, stout body

confuse.how: Smaller, with an upturned snout
Egg-eater has keeled rough scales, a small head and rasps instead of hissing

behaviour: A wetter-country snake at the edge of its range here; toads are its main food. Puffs up and hisses loudly.
bite: Painful swelling, rarely more. Antivenom not effective, not used: hospital for watching.
memo: A bigger night adder of wet places, rarely seen this far west.

size: Usually 2–3 m, up to 3.5 m and more
lives: Ground and low trees; termite mounds, hollow trees, rock piles
keys: Long, slender, grey to olive-brown, never black
Inside of the mouth inky black, shown in a gape when threatened
Long 'coffin-shaped' head with a pronounced brow
Smooth scales; lifts its front third off the ground

confuse.how: Boomslang has a short head and huge eyes, and lives in trees
Much smaller head, big eye and pale lip; the mouth is not black
Cobra is shorter and thicker and spreads a wide hood

behaviour: Keeps the same home for years, a termite mound or a hollow tree, and basks near it in the morning. Shy and quick to slip away; cornered, it rears up, spreads a narrow hood, gapes and strikes several times. Hunts dassies, squirrels, rodents and birds.
bite: Drooping eyelids, tingling, slurred speech and difficulty breathing, sometimes within 30 minutes. Firm pressure bandage over the whole limb, keep still, hospital as fast as possible; be ready to give mouth-to-mouth. The polyvalent antivenom works.
memo: Grey snake, black mouth, coffin head. Give it room and it leaves.

size: Usually 90 cm–1.2 m, up to 1.5 m
keys: Olive to slate-grey, scales often dark-edged
Salmon-pink to yellowish belly with black bars across the throat
Spreads a hood and spits venom at the eyes, up to 2–3 m
Often comes into houses and tents at night

confuse.how: Bigger, broader hood, one wide dark throat band; does not spit
Mamba is much longer and slimmer, with a narrow hood and black mouth

behaviour: The cobra most met at Pidwa. Hunts at night for toads, rodents, birds and other snakes, and enters buildings. Most bites are to people asleep on the ground. It rears, spits, then often plays dead.
bite: Painful swelling and blistering, can destroy tissue; rarely fatal. No pressure bandage: keep still, hospital. Spit in the eyes: rinse at once with plenty of water (or any bland liquid, even milk) for 10–15 minutes, do not rub, then see a doctor.
memo: Pink belly, black throat bars, spits: wear glasses near it, close the tent.

keys: Big, heavy cobra with a very wide hood
Yellow-brown to dark brown; a banded form has dark and yellow bands
One broad dark band across the throat
Does not spit

confuse.how: Smaller, with a salmon belly and several thin throat bars; it spits

behaviour: Keeps to a home termite mound and hunts toads, rodents, birds and eggs, which brings it to chicken runs. Rears high with the hood spread and hisses before it bites.
bite: Neurotoxic: drooping eyelids and trouble breathing. Firm pressure bandage, keep still, hospital fast, be ready to breathe for the victim. The polyvalent antivenom works.
memo: The big cobra with the broad hood; it stands its ground.

keys: Enlarged shield-like scale on the tip of the snout
Short, thick body with a short tail
Pinkish to grey-brown with dark blotches; black head and neck
Hisses, spreads a small hood and strikes when bothered

confuse.how: Grows far bigger, has no snout shield and spits

behaviour: Digs in sand with its shield and hunts frogs, lizards and rodents at night, often after rain. Puts on a good bluff, then plays dead.
bite: Pain, sometimes neurotoxic signs; serious bites are rare. No antivenom: pressure bandage, hospital.
memo: A little cobra with a shovel on its nose.

keys: Young ones boldly banded black and white
Adults uniform dark grey to black, the bands fading
Small head, blunt snout, small eyes

confuse.how: File snake has a triangular body with bare skin between the scales
Stiletto has a flat pointed head, a short spiked tail and no bands

behaviour: Seldom seen: it lives in burrows and comes up on warm wet nights to hunt other snakes, lizards and frogs. Slow, rarely bites.
bite: Pain and swelling, rarely more. No antivenom: hospital for watching.
memo: A banded youngster that turns black with age.

keys: Huge eyes on a short, egg-shaped head
Males bright green, or black above and yellow below; females olive to brown
Keeled scales; inflates its throat when threatened
Moves fast through branches, often seen raiding nests

confuse.how: Bush snake is smaller, with black spots on the front half and a flatter head
Twig snake is grey-brown, very thin, with a keyhole-shaped pupil
Mamba has small eyes in a long coffin-shaped head and lives mostly on the ground

behaviour: Hunts chameleons, lizards, birds and their eggs in the canopy, and is often found by the alarm calls of the birds mobbing it. Very shy; bites happen almost only when it is caught or handled.
bite: Little or nothing for hours, then bleeding from the gums and wounds, blood in the urine, up to 24–48 h later. Go to hospital even if there are no symptoms. No pressure bandage. A specific boomslang antivenom exists.
memo: Big eyes, short head, in the trees. Calm bite, slow killer: hospital anyway.

size: Usually 80 cm–1 m, up to 1.4 m
keys: Extremely thin, grey-brown like a twig, with pale and dark flecks
Horizontal keyhole-shaped pupil
Long lance-shaped head, top often green or speckled
Stays motionless with the front of the body held stiff in the air

confuse.how: Boomslang has a short head, a round pupil and is thicker
Mopane snake is much smaller, with a dark zigzag stripe down the back

behaviour: Waits in a bush, swaying like a twig in the wind, and grabs lizards, chameleons, frogs and birds. When threatened it inflates its throat, showing bright skin.
bite: Rare, but it can kill: bleeding problems as with the boomslang, and there is no antivenom. Hospital at once, even if there are no symptoms. No pressure bandage.
memo: A twig that looks at you through a keyhole.

lives: Underground, comes up on wet nights
keys: Uniform dark purple-brown to black, glossy
Flat head that does not stand out from the neck, small eyes
Short tail with a spike at the tip
Arches its neck, then strikes sideways or backwards

confuse.how: Very alike; the purple-glossed has a rounder head and a blunt tail with no spike
House snake has pale lines on the head and vertical pupils

behaviour: The 'side-stabbing' snake: its long fangs swing out to the side of the closed mouth, so it can bite even when held behind the head. Hunts other burrowing reptiles and rodent nests underground.
bite: Severe pain and swelling, sometimes tissue loss on the finger; not fatal to adults. No antivenom, no pressure bandage: hospital.
memo: Never pick up a small black snake: this one bites from any grip.

keys: Very slender with a long whip-like tail
Brown back with a dark-edged pale stripe along each side
Bright yellow belly and throat
Extremely fast; often just seen as a streak across the road

confuse.how: Duller, the stripes faint, the belly whitish
Bigger, uniform olive, with no bold stripes

behaviour: The snake most seen at Pidwa, crossing roads in the heat of the day. Hunts lizards by sight, often with the head raised over the grass. Breaks its tail easily if grabbed.
bite: Harmless to people: at most a little local pain.
memo: Stripes, yellow belly, and gone in a flash.

keys: Uniform olive-brown, some scales on the front dark-edged
Big eye over a pale yellowish lip
Long and fast, the head narrow

confuse.how: Mamba has a long coffin-shaped head with a small eye and a black mouth; a young mamba is the real look-alike, so keep away when unsure
Smaller, with bold side stripes and a yellow belly

behaviour: Hunts frogs, lizards, rodents and other snakes along rivers and pans. Bites readily if picked up.
bite: Some pain and swelling, no lasting effect.
memo: Olive and fast by the water: check the eye and the head before relaxing.

keys: Short blunt snout for a grass snake
Grey to olive-brown with faint pale side stripes
Whitish to pale yellow belly

confuse.how: Bolder stripes and a bright yellow belly

behaviour: A grassland grass snake, here at the edge of its range. Hunts lizards, rodents and small birds.
memo: A dull, short-nosed grass snake.

keys: Hooked, beak-like snout
Rufous to yellow-brown, a dark stripe through the eye
Stout for a racer, the eye large

confuse.how: Olive, with a pointed but not hooked snout

behaviour: Digs with its beak in sand and hunts rodents, lizards and other snakes in their burrows.
memo: The snake with a beak.

keys: Bright green with black spots or bars on the front half
Often bronze-brown towards the tail
Big golden eye, flat head
Climbs smooth walls and bark with ridged belly scales

confuse.how: Boomslang has a short rounded head with even bigger eyes and no black spots
Green snake is plain green with no spots, near water

behaviour: Hunts geckos and frogs in bushes and on buildings, and is often met in camp. Inflates its throat to show blue skin when cornered.
memo: Green with black spots: harmless, often the 'green mamba' people report.

keys: Plain bright green, no spots
White to yellowish belly
Slender, big eye

confuse.how: Bush snake has black spots on the front half
Boomslang has a short head with huge eyes and keeled scales

behaviour: Lives along rivers and dams, eating frogs and small fish.
memo: Plain green by the water.

keys: Uniform brown, from reddish to dark olive
Two pale lines on each side of the head, one through the eye
Vertical pupil, glossy smooth scales

confuse.how: Cobra is thicker with a pinkish belly and throat bars, and has no head lines
Stiletto is black-purple with a flat head and no head lines

behaviour: Hunts mice and rats around buildings and kills them by constriction: a good snake to have in camp.
memo: Brown with pale lines on the head: the camp's mouser.

keys: Flat head with a white stripe along the upper lip
Grey-brown to purple-black, the scales tipped white (peppered look)
Small eyes

confuse.how: Stiletto has no white tips to the scales and a short spiked tail

behaviour: Long front teeth for catching skinks and geckos asleep in their crevices.
memo: Peppered with white, teeth for skinks.

keys: Small, dark, with pale speckles forming blotches or bands
Flat head with a pale lip stripe

confuse.how: Bigger, evenly peppered rather than blotched

behaviour: A small skink hunter of rocky ground.
memo: A small, blotchy wolf snake.

keys: Uniform brown to olive, the belly pale yellow to salmon
Small head, smooth glossy scales
Found in and by the water

confuse.how: House snake has pale lines on the head and lives away from water

behaviour: Swims well and hunts frogs, tadpoles and small fish, which it constricts.
memo: The brown snake in the dam.

size: Usually 60 cm–1 m, up to 1.2 m
keys: Triangular in section, like a file
Dark grey to black, bare skin showing between keeled scales
Slow and gentle, almost never bites

confuse.how: Paler grey-brown with a cream stripe along the spine
Garter snake is round in section with smooth scales

behaviour: Eats other snakes and lizards.
memo: A black triangle-bodied snake that eats snakes.

lives: Ground, often near water and termite mounds
keys: Triangular body, grey to purple-brown
Cream stripe along the ridge of the spine
Pink skin showing between the scales

confuse.how: Black, smaller, without the pale spine stripe

behaviour: Hunts other snakes, venomous ones included, and seems unaffected by their venom.
memo: The striped file: kills cobras.

keys: Dark rhombic blotches along a grey-brown back, like a night adder
Small rounded head, rough keeled scales
Coils and rubs its scales together for a rasping hiss
Gapes a black mouth with no teeth to speak of

confuse.how: Night adder has a dark V on the head and smooth scales
Puff adder is far thicker, with a broad flat head and chevrons

behaviour: Eats only birds' eggs, swallowed whole: spines in the throat crack the shell, which it spits out. Fasts for months outside the nesting season.
memo: An adder look-alike that only eats eggs.

keys: Olive-grey with tiny white speckles
Upper lip red, orange, yellow or white
Head dark, glossy on top, wider than the neck
Flattens its head and strikes when threatened

confuse.how: House snake has pale head lines and a plain brown body

behaviour: Hunts frogs and toads at night around pans and camps. Puts on a fierce display, flattening and lifting the head and showing the lips.
memo: Coloured lips, fierce bluff, frog-eater.

keys: Orange to pinkish-buff with 20–40 dark cross-bars
Broad head, cat-like vertical pupil
Climbs well

confuse.how: Shield-nose is short and thick with a black head and a snout shield

behaviour: Hunts geckos, lizards and roosting birds, climbing walls and trees at night; often found in buildings.
memo: An orange snake with tiger bars and cat's eyes.

keys: Slender, pale grey-brown with darker marbled cross-bars
Big eyes with vertical pupils
Broad head on a thin neck

confuse.how: Tiger snake is orange with bold bars

behaviour: Hunts geckos and frogs in trees and under roofs at night.
memo: A night tree snake with big cat eyes.

keys: Small and thin, grey-brown like bark
Dark, zigzag-edged stripe down the back
Dark stripe through the eye

confuse.how: Twig snake is far longer, with a keyhole pupil and no back stripe

behaviour: Hunts geckos and lizards and their eggs under loose bark, especially on mopane and dead trees.
memo: A small zigzag-striped bark snake.

keys: Small, glossy dark brown to purple-grey
Flattened, sharp-edged shovel snout
Coils in a tight spiral when disturbed

confuse.how: Centipede-eater is pale brown with a black head and collar

behaviour: Digs for reptile eggs, especially gecko and lizard eggs, which it slits open.
memo: A tiny egg-thief with a shovel nose.

keys: Uniform purple-black with an iridescent sheen
Small eyes, rounded head
Short blunt tail

confuse.how: Stiletto has a flatter head and a spiked tail; treat both as stiletto

behaviour: Hunts burrowing snakes, blind snakes and legless skinks underground; surfaces after rain.
memo: Purple-black and glossy: hands off, it might be a stiletto.

keys: Small, pale red-brown to yellowish
Black head and a black collar on the neck

confuse.how: Grey-olive with a net pattern, black collar only

behaviour: Eats centipedes, subdued with venom; lives in old termite mounds.
memo: A small brown snake in a black hood.

keys: Grey-olive, each scale dark-edged in a net pattern
Black collar, sometimes a few bands behind it

confuse.how: Plain red-brown with a black head

behaviour: Hunts centipedes under rocks and in termite mounds.
memo: A netted small snake with a collar.

keys: Thick and cylindrical, the head and tail look alike
Sharp horny edge on the snout (the 'beak')
Eyes just dark dots under the scales; tail ends in a spine
Colour varies: blotched, speckled or plain

confuse.how: Thread snake is no thicker than a shoelace

behaviour: The world's biggest blind snake. Lives in termite and ant nests and eats their eggs and larvae; comes up in numbers after heavy rain.
bite: Not venomous, cannot bite a person.
memo: A shiny sausage with a beak, after the rain.

keys: Thin as a shoelace, glossy dark brown
Tail longer than in other thread snakes
Eyes as tiny black dots

confuse.how: Smaller, pinkish brown, with a short tail

behaviour: Follows ant and termite trails and eats their larvae.
memo: A worm with scales.

keys: Tiny and thin, pinkish brown and glossy
Short tail with a tiny spine
Moves smoothly, unlike an earthworm

confuse.how: Longer, darker, with a long tail

behaviour: Lives in termite nests and eats termites; surfaces after rain.
memo: Looks like an earthworm, shines like a snake.
